title: Are Rising Gold Prices Costing You on Every Repair?
text: Uncategorized Are Rising Gold Prices Costing You on Every Repair? If your pricing hasn’t changed since gold was $3,000, it’s not just outdated — it’s actively eroding your margins job by job. Published 2 days ago on May 21, 2026 By Jonathan Geller Instore June 2026 Issue Share Tweet IF YOU WROTE YOUR REPAIR PRICING when gold was $2,000-$3,000 and haven’t touched it since, you’re not just leaving money on the table: You’re actively losing it on every job that walks through your door. Gold doesn’t have to stay high forever to damage your margins. Services don’t have turn like inventory, so you don’t get another shot at it. Every job you quote at yesterday’s prices is a loss today, whether gold settles back next month or not. Build a Tier Before You Need It In repair and custom, the most effective move isn’t reacting to the market — it’s building a structure that lets you respond to it cleanly. In the Geller Blue Book, every SKU has an “Express” price listed just below the standard rate, and certain chapters have full replacement pages priced 50% higher tucked behind a “VIP” tab. When the market spikes, a store can swap to the higher-priced pages (and if a longtime customer balks, we can say, “Let me check the VIP pricing for you,” and give them the ORIGINAL price like it’s a favor). You don’t need the book to build this. Create a second price list for your most common metal-heavy repairs (sizing, shanks, clasps), call it whatever fits your culture, and have it ready. When the market justifies it, you flip. When a good customer needs some grace, you have something to offer without eating the margin yourself. Advertisement Train Your Staff on Why Advertisement Your team will get questions. When they do, gold at $4,500-5,000 is a gift for this conversation; it’s a headline your customers have already seen. A quick, confident explanation (“the metals market has moved significantly this year, and our pricing reflects that”) handled by a well-prepared professional lands better than any sign on your counter. Competition Pricing You Out? Not every store in your market has adjusted. Some are still sitting on old pricing, whether by choice, by inertia, or because they don’t know any better. That last one is worth thinking about, and your staff should be able to address it. A jeweler who hasn’t noticed that gold has nearly doubled since 2025 isn’t a bargain — they’re a question mark. If they’re charging that and keeping the lights on, where are they making it up, or what corners are they cutting along the way? Your heirloom ring deserves someone who knows what it costs to do the job right, charges accordingly, and isn’t quietly making it up somewhere else. That’s the story your team should be comfortable telling. Price for where the market is. Build a system that doesn’t require a fire drill every time gold moves. The jewelers who do that protect their margins no matter where it settles.
